contracts.commit_point: search_tool: the outbound request issued by await groq_client.chat.completions.create(model="groq/compound", ..., search_settings=...) at core/tools.py lines 170-185. scrape_tool: the outbound request issued by await client.get("https://api.scrape.do", params=params) at core/tools.py line 43, repeated per URL from the sequential loop at core/tools.py lines 92-100. A skip by the before_tool_callback prevents the tool function from executing, so these requests are never issued.
contracts.declared_mechanism: LlmAgent(before_tool_callback=create_combined_before_tool_callback(callback_cache, tool_max_calls)) at single_question_research_agent.py lines 778-780. create_combined_before_tool_callback (lines 477-489) instantiates create_enforce_query_deduplication_callback(cache) (lines 34-112) and create_enforce_tool_call_limits_callback(cache, tool_max_calls) (lines 115-157) and composes them via compose_before_tool_callbacks (lines 160-179), which awaits each callback in order and returns the first non-None dict, which per the framework's declared contract skips the tool. Per-agent budgets are built from priority_limits in the factory (lines 522-535) and passed into the callback registration.
contracts.forbidden_condition: (1) Executing a search_tool or scrape_tool invocation when the agent's cache counter f"{agent_name}_{tool_name}_calls" has already reached the priority-based maximum for that tool (high: search 4/scrape 2; medium: search 2/scrape 1; low: search 1/scrape 0); enforce_tool_call_limits must then return the non-None error dict "<tool_name> call limit reached" (lines 125-142). (2) Executing a search_tool invocation whose query embedding has cosine similarity >= COSINE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (0.85) against any previously stored query embedding for that agent; enforce_query_deduplication must then return the non-None error dict "Query is too similar to a previous query" (lines 88-99). Condition (2) applies only when tool.name == "search_tool" and a non-empty query arg is present (lines 46-51). Any non-None return from the composed callback short-circuits the remaining callbacks and skips the tool (lines 170-177).
pending_binding_information: That a non-None return from LlmAgent.before_tool_callback actually skips tool execution in google.adk rests on in-repo docstrings/comments (lines 121, 483-485); the framework source is not supplied.

That FunctionTool(search_tool).name == "search_tool" and FunctionTool(scrape_tool).name == "scrape_tool" (required to match the dedup check at line 46 and the budget dict keys at lines 28-31/532-535) depends on ADK FunctionTool naming behavior, which cannot be verified from the supplied source.

The call sites of create_single_question_research_agent — how many agents are instantiated per run and which "priority" values are passed — are not in the supplied views, so the concrete budgets in force at runtime are unconfirmed.
Whether any code path invokes search_tool or scrape_tool outside these agents' tool dispatch (which would bypass the guard) is not determinable from the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Model-driven tool invocations of groq_search_tool (FunctionTool wrapping search_tool) and scrape_websites_tool (FunctionTool wrapping scrape_tool) dispatched by the UnifiedResearchAgent LlmAgents, which register these tools at single_question_research_agent.py lines 774-777.
contracts.protected_resource: The agents' outbound external HTTP channels: the Groq compound web-search request (chat.completions.create with search_settings) and the scrape.do scraping request (GET https://api.scrape.do per URL) — i.e., each agent's bounded external web-search/scraping request budget and duplicate-free search issuance.
contracts.protection_obligation: The before_tool_callback registered on every per-question research LlmAgent (UnifiedResearchAgent) via create_combined_before_tool_callback, composing enforce_query_deduplication and enforce_tool_call_limits, must intercept and skip (block) model-driven invocations of the agent's search_tool (groq_search_tool) and scrape_tool (scrape_websites_tool) FunctionTools whenever the per-agent, per-tool call budget is exhausted or the search query is a semantic near-duplicate (cosine similarity >= 0.85), so that the tools' outbound Groq web-search and scrape.do HTTP requests are never issued. (Merged from both reviewer opinions, which restate the same composed-callback obligation.)
scope_limits: The guard covers only invocations dispatched through these LlmAgents' tool dispatch with the registered before_tool_callback; the supplied views show no other guarded call path for the tools.
The dedup condition is scoped to tool.name == "search_tool" with a non-empty "query" arg (lines 46-51); scrape_tool invocations are constrained only by the call budget.

Enforcement state is a per-agent-instance, process-local in-memory dict (callback_cache created at line 519) keyed by f"{agent_name}_{tool_name}_calls" (line 125) and f"{tool_name}_queries_embeddings" (line 60); it is not shared across agent instances, runs, or processes and is not persisted.

Dedup is best-effort: if embedding generation raises, the callback logs and returns None, permitting the query (lines 101-110); the current embedding is appended to the cache even when a duplicate is detected (lines 92-93).
The callback blocks by returning an error dict to the model (skip-with-feedback) rather than raising or terminating the agent.

Budget consumption is recorded at callback time (counter incremented at line 144 before execution) and depends on the factory's "priority" argument; low-priority agents have scrape_tool max 0, so every scrape attempt is blocked (lines 522-528). The module-level constants at lines 24-31 mirror the medium defaults, but the factory-built dict (lines 532-535) is the effective registered configuration.
Both guarded commit points share the http stratum; per the compilation rule, distinct-strata splitting does not apply and the two tools' commit points are covered by this single contract.
